personas.notes: Strong high-weight coverage: TypeScript, Node.js, SQL, TDD/JUnit, Git, AWS, Scrum, Kanban, CI/CD, Jenkins, React, HTML, CSS, SRE, post-mortems, financial systems, and Software Engineer title all appear. NestJS is only referenced obliquely ('modern backend frameworks (similar to NestJS)') in the LSEG bullet — an ATS exact-match on 'NestJS' (weight 1.0) will hit the word but the hedged phrasing weakens signal; add 'NestJS' plainly to the Framework skills line to guarantee capture. 'Logging' and 'alerting' (weight 0.5) are absent entirely — fold them into the SRE bullet ('...applying SRE practices, logging, alerting and post-mortems...'). 'Unit testing' as an exact phrase is missing; you have JUnit/Mockito/TDD but add 'unit testing' verbatim to the Tools line. must_mirror '2+ years as a Software Engineer' is technically satisfiable by the two SE roles but tenure math (June 2025–Jan 2026 plus 2022–2024) reads oddly for an MS expected Dec 2026 — the Dassault dates are in the future/overlap program, which dents plausibility. Formatting: LaTeX math glyph \vcenter/\hbox bullet and $\bullet$ render fine but the custom bullet macro plus heavy negative \vspace values (-18.5pt) can cause parser line-merging; standard \item bullets parse cleanly so risk is low. No tables or columns — good for ATS. Escaped ampersands (\&) are safe. Add a dedicated 'SQL-based databases' phrasing (you list PostgreSQL/NoSQL but not the JD's literal phrase) if you want exact must_mirror mirroring.

Strong keyword alignment — TDD, CI/CD, Jenkins, SRE, post-mortems, Scrum, Kanban, AWS, React/HTML/CSS, financial systems, and SQL are all present. But several plausibility red flags undercut the narrative. (1) The NestJS requirement is dodged with 'modern backend frameworks (similar to NestJS)' — if you've used NestJS, name it directly in a bullet and in Skills; the hedge reads as keyword-stuffing. (2) '99% test coverage' and 'Increased throughput 200%' and 'processing 1.4B daily records' are eye-poppingly round/large numbers with no context — I'd probe hard in interview. Ground them: 200% throughput measured how, baseline to what? 1.4B records in what system, and what was your specific ownership? (3) Seniority: JD wants mid-level (2+ yrs). Your LSEG role (Jul 2022–Aug 2024) provides ~2 yrs, which fits, but the Dassault role is only ~7 months and dated June 2025–Jan 2026 (future end date) while you're a full-time MS student expected Dec 2026 — that timeline strains credibility and needs clarification (internship? part-time?). Label it accordingly. (4) Impact bullets are decent action-verb-led but lean on percentages without the 'so what' — the Kafka-Elasticsearch bullet ('Boosted data retrieval 90% for 500+ analysts by applying Kanban') awkwardly bolts a process methodology onto a perf metric; separate the technical outcome from the Agile keyword. (5) 'GoonedIn' project name is unprofessional for a resume you'd hand a hiring manager — rename it. Overall the story of growth (finance backend → platform SWE → GenAI projects) is coherent and mid-level-appropriate; tighten the numbers and drop the NestJS hedge to move plausibility up.

Strong keyword coverage, but several claims won't survive a 30-min screen. RED FLAGS: (1) The LSEG bullet 'leveraging modern backend frameworks (similar to NestJS)' is a hedge that reads as keyword-stuffing — either you used NestJS or you didn't. NestJS is in must_mirror, so I'll probe it hard; parenthetical dodges signal you can't defend it. State the actual framework or claim NestJS directly if true. (2) '99% test coverage' is implausibly precise and pairing JUnit (Java) with Jasmine (JS) on the same 'robust microservices' needs a clear multi-language explanation — be ready to justify what each tested. (3) Dassault tenure June 2025–Jan 2026 is ~7 months yet claims a full microservices+CI/CD+recommendation POC portfolio; that's a lot for a short internship-length stint — tighten to what's genuinely defensible. (4) '1.4B daily records' AND '200% throughput' AND '90% data retrieval improvement' AND '75% recurrence reduction' — four large round-number metrics in one role reads as inflation. Be prepared to explain baseline/measurement for each; I'll ask 'how did you measure the 90%?' (5) 'two-tower embeddings' and 'AI-driven match scoring with DeepSeek' — make sure you can whiteboard the architecture, otherwise cut. STRENGTHS: TypeScript/Node/SQL/TDD/Git/AWS/Scrum/Kanban all present and mapped to real bullets. Financial-systems + SRE + post-mortems cleanly mirrored. AWS Solutions Architect *Professional* cert alongside 'Associate' is odd sequencing (Pro usually follows years of experience) — verify. ACTION: replace the 'similar to NestJS' hedge, soften one or two metrics with method context, and align cert claims with experience level.

Several framings are defensible but a few need tightening for a phone screen. LSEG bullet 'leveraging modern backend frameworks (similar to NestJS)' is a red flag — the source only shows Java/Spring Boot, no Node/NestJS server-side work at that role. This hedged phrasing ('similar to') will get probed and the candidate cannot claim NestJS experience honestly; the JD lists NestJS as a must_mirror item, so this is the weakest link. Recommend grounding TypeScript/Node/NestJS claims in the actual Node.js work (GoonedIn Next.js, LSEG React/Node monitoring dashboard) rather than implying NestJS on the financial platform. Dassault bullet 'Engineered robust microservices with 99% test coverage by applying TDD' — source says 'Maintained 99% test coverage,' which supports unit testing, but explicitly claiming TDD methodology goes beyond evidence; be ready to describe red-green-refactor or soften to 'unit testing.' 'Built service oriented systems' framing at LSEG is well-supported by the microservices/distributed systems evidence — plausible. Kanban/Scrum/SRE/post-mortem claims are consistent with the RCA/runbook source evidence — defensible. The two-tower embeddings recommendation POC, 1.4B records, and 200% throughput all trace cleanly to source. Overall the resume is credible for a mid-level SWE; the main interview risk is defending NestJS/TDD specifics that are adjacent-but-not-directly-evidenced.
